title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Maria Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood’s core people policies and practical guides for new and existing employees. It covers: how we work, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, an overview of the hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools you’ll use. This document is intended as a single reference for engineering, product, and cross-functional teams.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Short intro
Redwood values shipping reliable, production-first software and providing an engineering-first developer experience. We prioritize clarity, empathy, and ownership. The following sections summarize key day-to-day expectations and working norms.

Key principles
- Ship small, iterate quickly: prefer smaller PRs and frequent releases.
- Measurable ownership: every service and dashboard has a named owner and a documented SLO.
- Blameless postmortems: focus on systems and fixes, not individuals.
- Asynchronous-first communication: use docs and Confluence for decisions, Slack for lightweight coordination, and synchronous meetings when alignment is required.

Meeting & communication norms
- Daily standups are optional for most teams; use asynchronous updates unless your team is co-located or has high cross-dependency.
- Use the #engineering, #product, and #ops channels for cross-team announcements; use dedicated team channels for day-to-day work.
- All architecture decisions that affect other teams should be captured as an ADR in architecture-and-standards.

2) Roles and career ladders

Overview
Redwood uses level-based career ladders for Engineering, Product, Design, and SRE. Levels provide a consistent rubric for expectations, compensation calibration, and promotion discussions. Managers are responsible for level calibration during planning cycles; people-ops supports with calibration guidance.

Engineering ladder (summary table)
| Level | Typical years / signal | Core expectations |
|-------|-----------------------:|------------------|
| E1 - Associate Engineer | 0-2 years | Delivers scoped tickets, writes tests, works closely with mentor. |
| E2 - Engineer | 2-4 years | Owns medium-sized features, reliable code quality, participates in design reviews. |
| E3 - Senior Engineer | 4-8 years | Leads feature design, mentors others, responsible for service-level ownership. |
| E4 - Staff Engineer | 7+ years | Cross-team design leadership, drives technical strategy and major initiatives. |
| E5 - Principal/Distinguished | Career-level | Sets company-level architecture, mentors senior leaders, published design patterns. |

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate and manager prepare a promotion packet (examples in people-ops templates).
2. Packet goes to a calibration committee (peers + managers).
3. Committee returns decision and written feedback.
4. If approved, updated job level and compensation are applied in the next payroll cycle.

3) Benefits and perks

Health & wellbeing
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution tiers (details in benefits portal).
- Mental health resources: EAP, dedicated counseling reimbursement, and wellbeing stipends.

Compensation & equity
- Competitive base salary bands per level, annual performance review + merit cycle, and quarterly equity refresh for high performers.
- Transparent compensation FAQs available on the benefits portal.

Time off and parental leave
- Generous PTO policy (flexible time off) with recommended minimum of 15 days off per year.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks paid primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver.

Learning & development
- $2,000 annual learning stipend per employee for conferences, books, and courses.
- Internal mentorship program and quarterly brown-bag speaker series.

Office & remote work support
- Stipend for home office equipment and coworking allowance for remote-first employees.
- Hybrid office locations provide paid commuter benefits and on-site snacks.

Perks & culture programs
- Wellness days, team offsites (budgeted per team), and regular hack weeks.

4) Hiring overview — how we recruit and interview

Principles
- Hire for potential and impact: assess technical ability and ability to learn.
- Consistent candidate experience: timely feedback and clear communication from recruiters.
- Structured interviews: standard rubrics across roles and levels.

Typical hiring funnel (steps)
1. Resume screen by recruiter.
2. Hiring manager phone screen (30-45 minutes).
3. Technical interviews (coding, design, system design) with standardized rubrics.
4. On-site / final loop (typically 3-4 interviews + hiring manager debrief).
5. Offer and compensation calibration.

Interview feedback rubric (short)
- Technical competency: code quality, systems design, debugging.
- Product sense: ability to align tradeoffs with customer needs.
- Collaboration & communication: clarity, listening, and feedback.

Hiring checklist for interviewers
- Read candidate packet 24 hours before interview.
- Use the rubric and provide written feedback within 24 hours.
- Avoid questions that require non-work-safe topics or protected categories.

5) Onboarding — first 90 days checklist

Before day 1
- HR: sign offer, benefits enrollment, tax forms.
- IT: laptop order, access request submitted (people-ops triggers device order).

Day 1-7 (orientation)
- Orientation deck and company intro with People Ops.
- Team intro: 1:1 with manager, buddy assignment (buddy = peer for first 30 days).
- Accesses: GitHub, Slack, Confluence, JIRA, CI system, internal dashboards.

Week 2-4 (ramp)
- Complete onboarding tasks: local dev setup, run integration tests, make first small PR.
- Shadow support rotations and review runbooks relevant to your service.

Month 2-3 (impact)
- Own a small project or ticket and own deploy responsibilities with buddy.
- Review goals with manager and set 90-day objectives.

Onboarding checklist (numbered)
1. Confirm access to: Slack, GitHub, Confluence, JIRA, AWS/GCP console (if applicable).
2. Complete security training and SSO/MFA setup.
3. Complete payroll/benefits enrollment.
4. Schedule recurring 1:1s with manager and weekly check-ins with buddy for 30 days.

6) Internal tools guide — quick reference

We maintain a small number of core tools that every employee should know. Below is a quick-reference table and short how-tos.

Core tools table
| Tool | Purpose | First-run checklist |
|------|---------|--------------------|
| Slack | Team communication | Join #random, #engineering, your-team channel; set notification preferences. |
| Confluence | Documentation and handbooks | Follow People Ops space; bookmark team runbooks. |
| GitHub | Source control | Accept org invite, set up SSH key or token, join relevant repos. |
| JIRA | Issue tracking | Get project roles, add yourself to team board. |
| CI/CD (Buildkite) | Automated builds & deploys | Confirm deploy access, read deploy runbook. |
| Monitoring (Grafana/Prometheus) | Service metrics | Access dashboards for your services; subscribe to alerts. |
| PagerDuty | On-call & incident paging | Set escalation rules; follow on-call runbook. |

Quick how-tos (common tasks)
- Request a new repo: Open an Admin ticket in JIRA -> repos project with team name and README draft.
- Create a release: Follow release checklist in eng-platform/release-notes and tag in GitHub.
- Service incident: Follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process. Summon on-call via PagerDuty and notify #ops-incident channel.

Access & security
- All employees must enable SSO and MFA before critical accesses are granted.
- Least privilege applies; request elevated access with a time-bounded justification.

7) Additional resources and ownership

- People Ops (owner for handbook): people-ops@redwood.ai (for benefits, payroll, and policy questions).
- Engineering onboarding maintainer: eng-developer-experience team (see eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates).
- Security and compliance: security-and-compliance space for incident response and RBAC guidelines.

Document maintenance

- This page is owned by People Ops and reviewed quarterly. Suggested updates: email people-ops@redwood.ai or open a documentation PR in Confluence.

Appendix — common contact points
- HR / Benefits: people-ops@redwood.ai
- IT / Device requests: it-support@redwood.ai
- Payroll: payroll@redwood.ai
- On-call escalations: see PagerDuty runbooks in oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks

End of handbook summary.
